feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: the progression at NACo is clear, the scope is substantial, and the profile aligns well with strategy-heavy roles. It reads polished and modern, but impact would improve with more outcome-focused metrics, less repetition across skills sections, and a few wording/style fixes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression and credibility: multiple promotions at one organization show growth, trust, and increasing leadership scope.  
- Good strategic/technical blend: combines communications leadership with Drupal, analytics, workflow design, and multimedia production.  
- Generally strong writing: concise, professional tone with clear positioning around mission-driven, cross-channel communications.

1. Top improvements  
- Add sharper results: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than outcomes. Include more quantified impact beyond website size/traffic (e.g., engagement growth, efficiency gains, campaign results, revenue/member outcomes).  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap significantly. Consolidating would improve structure and scannability.  
- Fix style/consistency issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “12+ years of experience”; use serial commas consistently (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs later lists without final comma); “organization-wide” and “member-facing” are good, but punctuation in long dash-led bullets is dense—consider cleaner bullet formatting. No major misspellings found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It would be sharper with more specificity, a more current emphasis on strategy/platform transformation, and less overlap with the skills sections.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten the opening and fix style: use “12+ years of experience” instead of “more than 12 years experience.”
- Lead with seniority and sector relevance: emphasize digital strategy leadership for mission-driven/public-sector or advocacy organizations.
- Replace broad channel lists with higher-value differentiators such as platform modernization, governance, analytics, and workflow design.
- Add one concrete scope signal from recent roles, e.g., enterprise web platforms, cross-functional teams, or large-scale audience engagement.

Possible rewrite:
Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience guiding web, email, social, content, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Specializes in cross-channel strategy, platform modernization, digital governance, and workflow design that improve coordination, publishing efficiency, and audience engagement. Brings deep experience in advocacy communications, stakeholder alignment, and translating complex policy or technical topics into clear, accessible content.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant mix of strategic, technical, and communications capabilities, but several items overlap with the header and Topline Skills. Tightening the phrasing and reducing repetition will make this section feel sharper and more differentiated.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and tighten wording: “Digital strategy & transformation • Multi-channel communications • Web platform & CMS administration • Editorial workflow design • Analytics & performance reporting • Systems architecture & process improvement • Cross-functional stakeholder coordination • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia & live event production”
- Change “communication” to “communications” for consistency with the rest of the CV.
- Consider replacing the generic “Data analytics & reporting” with “Analytics & performance reporting” to better match senior-level impact.
- If space allows, prioritize more distinctive strengths such as “CMS modernization” or “Governance & publishing standards.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital strategy,” “multi-channel communications,” and “stakeholder coordination” repeat the header and Topline Skills.
- “Web & CMS administration” and analytics language also overlap with Technical + IT and Topline Skills.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, competencies, and project footer. Tighten it around 3–4 high-impact contributions and add outcomes, scale, or scope wherever possible.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper lead: “Embedded strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading web modernization, campaign delivery, and AI-enabled content discovery.”
- Replace generic verbs (“support,” “advise”) with ownership verbs: led, built, launched, redesigned, standardized, improved.
- Consolidate into 3–4 bullets, e.g.:
- Built Drupal-based campaign and storytelling experiences, including modular microsites, reusable content components, and downloadable member toolkits.
- Improved enterprise web operations by redesigning workflows, analytics, and publishing systems for coordinated cross-channel communications.
- Delivered front-end/CMS enhancements and troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties, strengthening usability and governance.
- Led an AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content workflows, and user-facing discovery.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI search and microsite work duplicate the “Recent Projects” section; keep this entry higher-level and reserve specifics there.
- “Governance/analytics/workflows” also echoes prior NACo roles—focus this item on what is new or elevated now.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management points already covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + leadership: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Combine the strongest achievements into sharper, outcome-led bullets: “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page Drupal website, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make impact more measurable where possible: add team size, budget, % efficiency gains, reporting adoption, production volume, or cost savings from the in-house studio.
- Tighten generic phrasing: replace “improving reporting and strategic decision-making” with a concrete result such as “standardized executive reporting” or “reduced manual reporting time.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership, platform modernization, analytics, and governance.
- Video-program language may duplicate older NACo roles; emphasize building the studio and scaling in-house production capacity instead.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps with both the later Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more specific to the operational/editorial leadership you owned at this stage, and tighten phrasing around outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + function: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial execution and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Combine newsletter bullets and sharpen impact: “Oversaw four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Reframe video bullet to show channel-building: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Replace vague workflow lines with one stronger bullet: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency and cross-team coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital publishing workflows” and “editorial coordination” overlap with the Director role’s governance/planning language.
- “Weekly video updates” repeats the earlier 2015–2018 role; emphasize scaling/operationalizing rather than originating.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline item overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should be tighter, more distinctive, and framed around leadership scope rather than repeating generic capability labels.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad nouns with sharper, outcome-oriented phrases:
- Enterprise digital strategy for public-sector organizations
- Editorial governance and scalable publishing systems
- Cross-channel communications leadership across web, email, social and video
- Advocacy and member-facing messaging strategy
- Audience-centered content planning and campaign storytelling
- Consider reducing to 4 bullets to improve scanability and avoid sounding repetitive.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie one phrase to scale (for example, “enterprise web and content operations for high-volume organizations”).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” duplicate Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” also repeats positioning already established in the header and multiple NACo roles.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and modernization themes, not every individual technology.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization” instead of listing multiple CMSs equally.
- Prioritize recent, differentiating strengths: Drupal, CMS modernization, API integrations, workflow automation, AI-enabled search.
- Trim lower-signal or older items here; move/share “WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, HTML/CSS/JavaScript/jQuery, Airtable systems” to Technical + IT only.
- Suggested rewrite: “- Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization - Front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting - API integrations and workflow automation - AI-enabled search and structured content experiences”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; avoid repeating exact platform/tool names in both places.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also overlaps with Core Competencies and Recent Projects, so keep it concise here.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a generic inventory rather than a senior-level capability statement. It should emphasize decision support, optimization, and business impact—especially since recent roles already show hands-on ownership of the analytics stack.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from tool list to outcome-oriented skill cluster, e.g.: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio & Microsoft Clarity for analytics infrastructure, KPI design, executive reporting and digital performance optimization”
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with “Executive dashboards and decision support” for sharper, more senior phrasing.
- Consider changing “SEO and performance analysis” to “SEO, UX and content performance analysis” if accurate; it better reflects Clarity and broader optimization work.
- Keep to 5–7 items max; example: “GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI & Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • KPI design • Executive dashboards • SEO/UX performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This overlaps heavily with “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization”; keep Topline Skills more strategic and let Technical + IT hold the full tool list.
- “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating that exact phrasing.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and older NACo experience. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities and make the phrasing more senior and distinctive.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic nouns with sharper, grouped terms: “Broadcast video production & editing • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and studio systems • Virtual event operations”
- Consider adding a leadership/operations angle to match recent roles: “In-house studio buildout and broadcast workflows” or “Studio and livestream operations”
- Drop “virtual” if keeping “hybrid event delivery,” or combine them to avoid padding: “Hybrid/virtual event production”
- If space allows, align to outcomes rather than tasks: “Broadcast-quality video production” instead of “Video production and editing”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; use this section for more specific tools/systems, not the same wording.
- “Studio operations” and “PTZ camera systems” are useful differentiators; keep those over broader, repeated phrases.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This item should either be tightened to emphasize strongest/recent platforms or add light qualifiers that reinforce seniority and modernization work.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Better: **Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, signal level rather than just naming tools: **Enterprise CMS platforms: Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages**
- Keep GitHub Pages only if it reflects meaningful professional use; otherwise replace with a stronger platform or remove for concision.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider trimming one section or using this item for platform names only and the other for broader capabilities.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent roles, so avoid repeating extra Drupal detail elsewhere unless tied to outcomes.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools actually used in recent roles and group items more clearly.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: “HTML/CSS • JavaScript/jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions”
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless the CV is targeting hands-on developer roles; they add little value at this level.
- Consider ordering by relevance to recent work: “API integrations • GTM • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions • HTML/CSS • JavaScript/jQuery”
- If accurate, replace one generic item with a stronger qualifier, e.g. “custom front-end implementation” or “serverless scripting (Cloudflare Workers)” to better match recent Drupal/search work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Workflow automation” appears elsewhere; avoid implying GitHub Actions is a major differentiator unless supported by project bullets.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems leadership. Since “workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear elsewhere, this item should be tighter and more implementation-focused.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe by function, not just brand names: “Workflow automation & work management: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier; project operations: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp; team collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams.”
- Put the strongest, most relevant tools first: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana.
- If true, add scope in parentheses to show applied use: “Airtable (workflow databases), Power Automate/Zapier (cross-platform automations), Jira/Asana (editorial and project tracking).”
- Consider shortening to 6–7 tools max and dropping weaker/older overlaps like Basecamp or Trello if space is tight.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies/Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Slack and Teams are common collaboration tools; they add less differentiation than automation/build tools.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as generic software inventory rather than evidence of email/engagement capability. Since email leadership already appears strongly in recent NACo roles, this item should stay concise and tool-focused.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten platform naming for readability: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add one capability layer instead of more tools: **campaign automation, newsletter operations, audience segmentation**
- Optional stronger version: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp | Email campaign automation, newsletter publishing, audience segmentation**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating outcomes like “tens of thousands reached” here; those are already covered well in recent work experience.
- Don’t add broad “multi-channel communications” language; that’s already prominent in Core Competencies and role descriptions.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with concrete outputs if you can quantify them.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-team building and hands-on production: “Promoted across two digital roles while helping establish NACo’s first in-house digital team and standardize workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add 1–2 measurable outcomes if available: size/timing of website refresh, number of livestreams or weekly videos produced, audience growth, email/social engagement, or team/process improvements.
- Tighten the close to show scope and supervision: “Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate.”
- If space allows, split into two bullets rather than one dense paragraph.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 advocacy video bullet; distinguish this as the earlier launch/build phase.
- “Strengthening workflows” repeats later governance/operations themes; keep this version tactical, not strategic.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a notable “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo digital/media roles. Emphasize innovation/program support and keep the digital piece concise.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to foreground cross-functional coordination and the standout launch: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo program and policy teams.”
- Tighten the second sentence and make the podcast the proof point: “Produced digital and multimedia content, including launching NACo’s first podcast and leading planning, scripting, and production.”
- If you can, add scope or outcomes: number of projects supported, audiences reached, episodes produced, or how the podcast supported member engagement/policy communications.
- Consider a sharper full rewrite: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives for NACo program and policy teams, while supporting digital content and multimedia production. Launched the organization’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, and production.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this higher-level and avoid repeating video/content operations language.
- Don’t overstate digital leadership here since stronger, more recent NACo roles already cover that progression.
